clue.text: Reversing engine component requiring skills in basic vehicles

indicators.note: reversing tells us to read the engine part from right to left

parts.note: a cog is a toothed wheel in an engine's gearing
arts are skills, as in the arts of persuasion

explanation.surface: A mechanic says fixing a reverse gear part in simple cars takes some know-how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' turns COG into GOC; 'requiring' is just a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Small open motor vehicles with very simple construction, raced on tracks for fun, are synonymous with this answer.

clue.text: Information about a heartless left-wing plot

indicators.note: about says the information word wraps around the middle pieces

parts.note: gen is informal British for information

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the political word

parts.note: red describes left-wing politics

explanation.surface: Intelligence concerning a cruel socialist conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle E of the political colour; 'plot' looks like a scheme but is a patch of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot is a small piece of ground, such as a cultivated yard.

clue.text: Comment attributed to one getting shot?

definitions.text: Comment attributed to one getting shot?

parts.words: Comment attributed to one getting shot?
parts.note: a photographer asks the subject to say this dairy word to make them smile for the shot

explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests gunfire, but it is a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying this word shapes the mouth into a smile for a photo, a remark expected of the subject.

clue.text: Card game in a poor state with no Clubs

indicators.note: with no says a letter is to be removed

parts.note: crummy is informal for shabby, in poor condition
C is the card-playing abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A card game played with a battered pack that has lost its clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A game where players collect sets and sequences of cards is a classic card game.

clue.text: Complete coverage put in place for opening day of time required

indicators.note: put in place for opening says the first letter is swapped out for the new piece

parts.note: duration is the length of time needed for something
Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday, a day

explanation.surface: Total insurance cover is set up for opening day of a long-term project.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT replaces D, the opening letter of DURATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturation means filling something to capacity, a thorough blanket coverage, as in saturation bombing or advertising.

clue.text: Dog inflicting wound, say, that is dragged back

parts.note: something sharp, like a blade, is an example of a thing that wounds

indicators.note: dragged back means the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A dog bites someone and then gets hauled off by its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dragged back' turns IE into EI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese breed with a wrinkled skin and blue-black tongue is a kind of canine.

clue.text: As usual, lacking time to make footwear

indicators.note: lacking means a letter is missing from the word

parts.note: stock means standard or usual, as in a stock answer

explanation.surface: As always, short of time to make shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted covering for the foot worn inside a shoe is a piece of footwear.

clue.text: Delectable doctor embraced by a sailor at sea

indicators.note: embraced by says the doctor is held inside the letters that follow
at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A tasty medic is hugged by a seaman on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' jumbles the sailor's letters; MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the doctor held inside after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the gods, so something like it is delicious or delightful.

clue.text: Mannerism during call regarding the way speech sounds

indicators.note: during places the mannerism within the time of the call, here at its end

parts.note: to phone someone is to call them
a tic is a habitual twitch or mannerism

explanation.surface: Someone has a habitual twitch while on the telephone, affecting how they talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetics is the study of speech sounds, so this adjective concerns how speech is pronounced.

clue.text: Sounds of bells initially ignored in Oxford literary group

indicators.note: initially ignored says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: tinklings are the light ringing sounds of small bells

explanation.surface: Chimes go unheeded in an Oxford writers' circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the group was the circle of C.S. Lewis and J.R.R. Tolkien.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name of an informal club of Oxford writers, including Tolkien and C.S. Lewis.

clue.text: Sadly irate with much of joint pain

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone is miserably cross about how much their arthritic joints hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is just a link; the fodder is IRATE plus MUCH, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes aching or inflammation in the joints, as in rheumatism.

clue.text: Tolerate two chessmen

parts.note: two signals a pair of pieces; the first is B, chess notation for a bishop
the second piece is the rook, or castle

explanation.surface: A chess player puts up with having just a pair of pieces left.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something is to put up with it, usually in a negative such as 'brook no argument'.

clue.text: They try bridge opponents and crime writer

parts.note: in bridge East and South sit against each other, so E and S are opponents
Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels

explanation.surface: A list of people who have a go at bridge, some opponents, and a detective novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South and East-West are partnerships, so E and S are on opposing sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay is to attempt, so those who attempt things are people making a try.

clue.text: Mushrooms: quickly eat one around end of course

indicators.note: around says the first pieces go about the extra letter

parts.note: to bolt food is to gulp it down fast

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of course

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Advice to wolf down the mushroom dish as the meal comes to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts E, the last letter of 'course', inside BOLT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin plural of the genus name for porcini and similar fleshy fungi.

clue.text: High jinks and at it when going round a region of Asia

indicators.note: going round says the jumbled letters surround a single letter
high, as in intoxicated, says the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Riotous fun and games when touring part of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' rearranges JINKS AT IT; 'and' and 'when' are links, and 'going round' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Central Asian republic, formerly part of the Soviet Union, so a region of that continent.

clue.text: Creating room for second arrangement of initial gaps

indicators.note: arrangement of tells us the letters that follow are to be reordered

explanation.surface: Leaving room for a second layout of the first spaces in a design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; S comes first, then INITIAL GAPS reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things in space, making distinct areas, is to set out room, a spatial process.

clue.text: Support includes this, working to secure new book producer?

indicators.note: includes says the support word wraps around what follows

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: to secure means the jumbled letters hold another letter fast inside
working means in operation, a signal that the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: The support includes this item, set up to secure a new book producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' jumbles the word this to INTSH around N; 'includes' puts that inside the support word.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where printing is done produces books among other things; the question mark admits the loose fit.

clue.text: Wine's raised before sign of drunkenness in song

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: ports are fortified wines, the 's read as a plural
hic is the hiccup of someone drunk

explanation.surface: Glasses of wine are lifted before the drinker hiccups into a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns PORTS into STROP.
explanation.definitionFit: A strophic song repeats the same music for each verse, so the term applies to song structure.

clue.text: Hors d'oeuvres? Some rubbish I fixed up

parts.note: crud is slang for dirt or rubbish

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: set means fixed, as in set in place

explanation.surface: Someone serves starters that are partly junk they threw together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SET into TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw vegetable sticks served with dips are a kind of starter served before a meal.

clue.text: Rioter's trial involved soldiers

indicators.note: involved suggests something tangled, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Troops were drafted in during the court case of a rioter.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored: RIOTERS TRIAL is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the British Territorial Army, its part-time reserve, are soldiers.

clue.text: Follow soldiers to design uniform?

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Copying the troops in order to create a new uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor is to cut and make clothing, such as a uniform, to fit.

clue.text: 75% of Lakeland trips … come here?

indicators.note: trips, as in stumbles, tells us the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
75% of an eight-letter word keeps its final six letters, cutting the opening two

explanation.surface: Three quarters of visits to the Lake District pass through this town.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting LA leaves KELAND, which 'trips' reorders; the whole clue then describes the town, a gateway to the Lake District in Cumbria, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This market town on the edge of the Lake District is where many tourist trips arrive.

clue.text: Strange thing recalled party song (though not repeated element)

indicators.note: recalled, as in called back, says the word for party is turned around

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: the doubled letter in the song word appears only once, one of its pair dropped

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A curious party anthem whose chorus is not sung twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns DO into OD; 'not repeated element' drops one T of DITTY's doubled T, leaving DITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odd or peculiar is a curiosity, a strange specimen.

clue.text: Suggestion overdue about new form of treated metal

indicators.note: about says the first word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice or suggestion
late means behind time, overdue

explanation.surface: A belated suggestion about a new way to process metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the suggestion around N, before the overdue word is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheet iron or steel coated with tin is a treated metal, used for cans.

clue.text: Entry from Sachs in Prize Song

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the prize word

parts.note: the palm is a prize of victory, as in bear the palm

indicators.note: entry from takes the first letter, the way in

explanation.surface: Hans Sachs makes an entrance in the Prize Song, from Wagner's Meistersinger.
explanation.walkthrough: Hans Sachs is the cobbler-poet in Wagner's opera, which features a Prize Song: S goes inside PALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, as in the Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Author having no time finally for his compatriot

indicators.note: having no means the letter is removed from the author's name

parts.note: Sir Walter Scott was a Scottish novelist

explanation.surface: A writer short of time in the end writes for a fellow countryman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' says the T taken from SCOTT is the last one; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott was from Scotland, so his fellow countryman is a native of that nation.

clue.text: Come out from access point?

definitions.meaning: chicks come out of their eggs when they break through the shell
a trapdoor or opening in a deck or floor gives access

explanation.definitionFit: A chick emerging from its shell, and an opening such as a ship's trapdoor, share this word.

clue.text: Conservative not initially irritated after Whip jeered

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation and remaining word behind the whip

parts.note: a cat, or cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

indicators.note: not initially means the opening letter is taken away

parts.note: galled means annoyed or irritated

explanation.surface: An annoyed Tory heckles once the party's whip has spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' is a parliamentary officer on the surface but the cat-o'-nine-tails here; 'not initially' drops G from GALLED to leave ALLED.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out with whistles and derisive shouts at a performer is to jeer.

clue.text: Rubbish heaps dry after sending back wet waste?

indicators.note: sending back says the whole string of letters is written backwards

parts.note: tips are dumps where rubbish is heaped
sec is French for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: Dumps dry out after damp refuse is returned to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry after' sets the dry word after the heaps; 'sending back' then turns the whole run around. The definition is a cryptic hint at sewage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit receiving sewage and liquid refuse is a store of wet waste.

clue.text: Figure left behind when mines were union-dominated?

indicators.note: behind places the abbreviation for left at the end

parts.note: the NUM, National Union of Mineworkers, was the powerful British miners' union
an era is a time, the period when something held

explanation.surface: A figure stranded once the coal mines were run by the union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when mines were union-dominated' reads as the NUM ERA; the NUM was the National Union of Mineworkers, dominant in British coalfields until the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a symbol for a number, i.e. a figure such as 7 or VII.
